newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SHK Prop says sees higher year results.
newsitem.headline: SHK Prop says sees higher year results.

text.p: Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd said on Thursday it expects "considerable growth" for its full year results.

"Most residential properties scheduled for completion in the current financial year have been presold. With a buoyant property market, the group's results for the current year are expected to show considerable growth," chairman and chief executive Walter Kwok said in a statement accompanying the company's interim results.
Kwok said Sun Hung Kai Properties was optimistic about the prospects for the residential property market in Hong Kong.

Residential property prices went up an average of 30 percent during 1996, mainly due to tight supply and strong demand, he said, adding that with rising income, low interest rates and population growth, demand for housing would remain strong.

In view of the recent higher level of speculative activity, Sun Hung Kai Properties would continue to cooperate with the government and adopt measures to curb speculation when launching new projects for sale, Kwok said.
But he urged to government to relax the 12-month presale period for new projects so that the immediate availability of residential units would increase.

Kwok said the group's land bank, acquired at a cost substantially below current market prices, was sufficient for its development needs in the next five years, but added it will continue to acquire new sites on a selective basis.

Sung Hung Kai Properties would continue to develop a diverse portfolio of properties in Hong Kong, and would invest more in new prestigious rental properties and infrastrucure projects to achieve its long-term objective of an equal balance between development profit and recurrent income, he said.
The group was in a strong financial position with low gearing and a significant recurrent income base, Kwok said.

With substantial liquidity and increasing confidence within the Hong Kong financing markets, the group had recently procured new banking facilities at more favourable terms to replace existing ones, he said.
The group's liquidity would be enhanced by the launch soon of projects such as Parkside Villa and Ha Yau Tin in Yuen Long, TLTL 66 in Tsing Lung Tau and Lam Tei in Tuen Mun, he added.
Kwok also noted the favourable macro outlook, including prospects for China's and Hong Kong's economies.
Investment and spending were up as confidence rose towards Hong Kong handover to China on July 1, which was also expected to benefit the tourist industry, he said.
Office rentals were expected to reman at a reasonable level, helping Hong Kong maintain its position as an international business centre, he added.
